plan.estimand: Mean weight reduction from baseline to follow-up
plan.hypothesis: H₀: μ_difference = 0 kg vs H₁: μ_difference = 3 kg (one-sided, testing superiority of weight reduction)
assumptions: Differences between baseline and follow-up weight are approximately normally distributed
Within-person correlation (r) between baseline and follow-up measurements is 0.5
Weight changes are independent across participants
No attrition or loss to follow-up
scientific_notes: Paired t-test uses the standard error of paired differences
This accounts for the correlation structure in repeated measurements

answer.summary: For a paired t-test detecting a 3-kg mean weight reduction with baseline SD 5 kg, follow-up SD 5.5 kg, within-person correlation 0.5, one-sided test at α = 0.05, the minimum integer sample size achieving 80% power is **21 participants**. This yields achieved power of 0.8092 (80.92%). At n = 20, power falls to 0.7909 (79.09%), below the 80% target.
answer.method: Paired t-test via stats::power.t.test with type="paired" and alternative="one.sided". Standard deviation of paired differences calculated as √(SD₁² + SD₂² − 2·r·SD₁·SD₂) = √(25 + 30.25 − 2·0.5·5·5.5) = 5.2678 kg. Effect size (delta) = 3/5.2678 = 0.5695. Sample size inverted from target power of 0.8, then rounded up to the next integer and verified.

Within-person correlation between baseline and follow-up is constant at 0.5

limitations: Sample size calculation assumes no missing data; in practice 10-15% attrition is common in weight-loss studies

Effect size is fixed; heterogeneity of treatment response across participants is not modeled
Assumes specified SDs and correlation are accurately known from prior data or pilot studies

# Paired t-test sample size calculation
# H0: mu_difference = 0 vs H1: mu_difference = 3 kg (one-sided)
# Alpha = 0.05, Target Power = 0.8

# Given parameters
mean_difference <- 3      # kg
sd_baseline <- 5          # kg
sd_followup <- 5.5        # kg
r <- 0.5                  # within-person correlation
alpha <- 0.05             # significance level
power_target <- 0.8       # target power
one_sided <- TRUE         # one-sided test

# Calculate SD of paired differences
# SD_diff = sqrt(SD1^2 + SD2^2 - 2*r*SD1*SD2)
sd_diff <- sqrt(sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2*r*sd_baseline*sd_followup)

cat("SD of paired differences:", sd_diff, "kg\n")

# For paired t-test, we use stats::power.t.test
# The effect size (delta) is the mean difference in units of SD of differences
effect_size <- mean_difference / sd_diff
cat("Effect size (delta):", effect_size, "\n")

# Use power.t.test with type="paired"
# For one-sided test, we need to account for this in the alpha parameter
# power.t.test uses two-sided alpha by default, so for one-sided we use alpha/2? 
# Actually, power.t.test has a one.sided parameter
result <- power.t.test(
  n = NULL,
  delta = mean_difference,
  sd = sd_diff,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = power_target,
  type = "paired",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("\n=== Sample Size Calculation ===\n")
cat("Mean difference:", mean_difference, "kg\n")
cat("SD of differences:", sd_diff, "kg\n")
cat("Alpha (one-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n")
cat("Exact sample size:", result$n, "\n")

# Round up to next integer
n_min <- ceiling(result$n)
cat("Minimum integer sample size:", n_min, "\n")

# Verify achieved power at minimum integer sample size
power_achieved <- power.t.test(
  n = n_min,
  delta = mean_difference,
  sd = sd_diff,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "paired",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

cat("\nAchieved power at n =", n_min, ":", power_achieved, "\n")

# Also check power at n-1 for reference
if (n_min > 1) {
  power_prev <- power.t.test(
    n = n_min - 1,
    delta = mean_difference,
    sd = sd_diff,
    sig.level = alpha,
    type = "paired",
    alternative = "one.sided"
  )$power
  
  cat("Power at n =", n_min - 1, ":", power_prev, "\n")
}

# Return results as JSON
results <- list(
  sample_size = n_min,
  sample_size_unit = "participants_total",
  exact_solution = result$n,
  achieved_power = power_achieved,
  sd_differences = sd_diff,
  effect_size = effect_size,
  parameters = list(
    mean_difference_kg = mean_difference,
    sd_baseline_kg = sd_baseline,
    sd_followup_kg = sd_followup,
    within_person_correlation = r,
    alpha_one_sided = alpha,
    target_power = power_target
  )
)

cat("\n=== FINAL RESULTS ===\n")
print(jsonlite::toJSON(list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_min, unit = "participants_total"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_achieved, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "power_at_n_minus_1", value = if(n_min > 1) round(power_prev, 4) else NA, unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "sd_differences", value = round(sd_diff, 4), unit = "kg"),
    list(metric = "effect_size", value = round(effect_size, 4), unit = "unitless")
  )
), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
